**git-sync `e9532731` — the fix.** `runReplicate` now routes on the resume marker's presence, ahead of the emptiness heuristic: a surviving `refs/gitsync/bootstrap/*` ref plus all desired target refs absent sends the run to the bootstrap strategy (new relay reason `bootstrap-resume-marker`, reported by dry-run too), where the existing `ResumeHash`/chain-position machinery picks up from the exact checkpoint. Stray refs no longer re-wedge the repo, matching the ticket's robustness argument. On the partial shape bootstrap can't take (some branch complete, another mid-flight), replicate's prune now skips live markers so resume state is never destroyed. **mirror-pipeline `9b2fed3` — the ticket's follow-up.** "Sync complete" now logs `operation_mode`, `transfer_mode`, `relay_reason`, so a wrongly-routed repo is one log query away. Works with the current git-sync pin.

- **Dropped the deletes-before-updates reorder in `replicate.Execute`.** The update-then-delete order is load-bearing for the worker's default-branch rename recovery (`cmd/worker/defaultbranch.go:67`): the deny-current-branch rejection must fire only after the replacement branch exists, or recovery calls `SetDefaultBranch` on an absent branch. With routing fixed, marker cleanup no longer gates anything. Advisor concurred after seeing the evidence.
- **Skipped the `excludeRefPrefixes` stopgap** — it would block stale-marker pruning forever and saves no deploy, since both ship via a mirror-pipeline release anyway.
- **One caveat for the PR:** small repos (rci-shaped, under the 1.5 GiB GitHub preflight threshold with `TargetMaxPackBytes` unset) take the one-shot bootstrap path — a full re-transfer rather than a literal resume, with the marker pruned on the following run. Convergent, just not incremental.

gh pr create --repo entireio/git-sync --head nodo/ent-2054-interrupted-batched-bootstrap-can-never-resume-the-resume --title "Route replicate to bootstrap when a resume marker survives on the target" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
Fixes [ENT-2054](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-2054/interrupted-batched-bootstrap-can-never-resume-the-resume-ref) — an interrupted batched bootstrap could never resume, because its own resume marker disqualified the bootstrap route. [ENT-1948](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1948/mirror-sync-permanently-fails-when-catch-up-pack-exceeds-10-gib) is one instance.

## The bug

Batched bootstrap writes `refs/gitsync/bootstrap/heads/<branch>` so an interrupted run can resume. Under `replicate --all-refs --prune` (the mirror-worker shape), that marker was just an undesired target ref of `RefKindOther`, so `replicateCanBootstrap` returned false and every subsequent sync routed to `replicate` — a single unbatched pack. The artifact of the one strategy that can resume is exactly what locked that strategy out, permanently.

## The fix

`replicateBootstrapRoute` now routes on the marker's presence, ahead of the emptiness heuristic. The namespace has exactly one writer — batched bootstrap, which deletes its marker on finalize or when stale — so a surviving marker is a positive signal: a bootstrap started and did not finish. The route requires every desired target ref to be absent (the bootstrap planner refuses targets whose desired refs exist) and deliberately ignores other stray target refs, so an aborted push or a branch deleted upstream mid-bootstrap cannot re-wedge the repo. The new reason `bootstrap-resume-marker` is threaded through dry-run too, so a plan against a stranded repo confirms the routing in one shot.

On the one partial shape the route cannot take (some desired branch complete, another mid-flight), replicate stays the executor; its prune plans now skip markers that still carry resume state (`dropLiveBootstrapMarkerDeletes`), so a best-effort run whose branch create is individually rejected cannot destroy the resume position. Markers whose branch exists or left the desired set stay prunable — replicate's prune is the only cleaner stale markers have.

## Deliberately not done

- **Deletes-before-updates in `replicate.Execute`** (floated in the ticket): the update-then-delete order is load-bearing for mirror-worker's default-branch rename recovery (`cmd/worker/defaultbranch.go:67`, recovery at `cmd/worker/syncer.go:464` in mirror-pipeline), which relies on the replacement branch existing before entiredb rejects the current-branch delete. Reordering would fire that rejection with the replacement absent and `SetDefaultBranch` would target a branch the mirror doesn't have. With routing fixed, marker cleanup no longer gates anything, so the reorder's benefit is cosmetic while its risk touches a recovery contract.
- **The `excludeRefPrefixes` stopgap in mirror-worker**: hiding `refs/gitsync/` from the sync scope would block stale-marker pruning forever, and it saves no deploy — stopgap and real fix both ship via a mirror-pipeline release.

## Caveats

- Small repos below the 1.5 GiB GitHub preflight threshold (with `TargetMaxPackBytes` unset) take the one-shot bootstrap path: a full re-transfer rather than a literal resume, with the marker pruned on the following run. Convergent — not a resume bug.
- The stranded repos (`gh/nicschick/vc3r`, `gh/nicschick/rci`) heal only once mirror-pipeline's git-sync pin is bumped past this and deployed. The companion observability change (logging `operation_mode`/`transfer_mode`/`relay_reason` from the worker) is independent and already on the same-named mirror-pipeline branch.

input.description:
Fast-follow to ENT-2054 (git-sync PR [#116](https://github.com/entireio/git-sync/pull/116)). That PR makes an interrupted batched bootstrap resumable from its `refs/gitsync/bootstrap/*` marker under replicate, but two shapes remain outside the resume route — both surfaced and confirmed by the PR's code review.

## 1. Partial-progress resume (the sharpened remainder of the original wedge)

`replicateBootstrapRoute` requires **all** desired target refs to be absent, because `BuildBootstrapPlans` refuses targets whose desired refs exist. A multi-branch bootstrap interrupted **after any branch finalized** (trunk done, secondary branch mid-flight) therefore can never resume batching: the remaining branch goes as one unsubdividable replicate pack. The live marker is preserved and anchors the delta (PR #116's prune guard), so the pack shrinks relative to a fresh transfer — but if the residual delta exceeds the target's pack cap, the repo wedges exactly like ENT-2054.

Fix shape: subset bootstrap — when a live marker exists and *some* desired refs are absent, route only the absent subset through the bootstrap strategy (existing target refs already serve as haves via `completedRefs`). Needs decisions on mixed-run semantics: what the Result reports, that prune is skipped for the run, and that present branches stay stale until the next delivery (a dormant upstream means no next delivery — consider a follow-up kick).

## 2. Sync mode has no resume route at all

The routing lives in the replicate-only syncer method; `sync --all-refs --prune` against a marker-bearing target still disqualifies bootstrap via `planner.CanBootstrapRelay` (prune disables it outright, `relay.go`). Same wedge shape as the original ticket, different mode. PR #116 only fixed sync mode's destructive half (its prune no longer deletes live markers, via the shared `addPruneCandidates` exception). Wants the marker routing hoisted somewhere both modes share — likely the planner.

## Smaller items to sweep into whichever change touches the area

- **Stale marker under `Mappings` or branch-scoped prune has no cleaner**: `PruneTarget` only selects `RefKindOther` under AllRefs-without-Mappings, so an interrupted `--map` run leaves a marker that lingers forever (it no longer misroutes anything after PR #116's orphan fix — it just persists).
- **Dry-run doesn't disclose the one-shot path's marker deletes** (consistent with the batched temp-ref lifecycle, which dry-run also omits) — fold in if plan reporting is touched.
- **Reviewer suggestion**: the non-batchable-source integration test asserts the marker survives but not that it was sent as a fetch have; add the assertion if the test server grows negotiation capture.

Fixes [ENT-2054](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-2054/interrupted-batched-bootstrap-can-never-resume-the-resume-ref) — an interrupted batched bootstrap could never resume, because its own resume marker disqualified the bootstrap route. [ENT-1948](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-1948/mirror-sync-permanently-fails-when-catch-up-pack-exceeds-10-gib) is one instance.

## The bug

Batched bootstrap writes `refs/gitsync/bootstrap/heads/<branch>` so an interrupted run can resume. Under `replicate --all-refs --prune` (the mirror-worker shape), that marker was just an undesired target ref of `RefKindOther`, so `replicateCanBootstrap` returned false and every subsequent sync routed to `replicate` — a single unbatched pack. The artifact of the one strategy that can resume is exactly what locked that strategy out, permanently.

## The fix

`replicateBootstrapRoute` routes on the marker's presence, ahead of the emptiness heuristic. The namespace has exactly one writer — batched bootstrap, which deletes its marker on finalize or when stale — so a surviving marker for a branch **in the desired set** is a positive signal: a bootstrap started and did not finish. The route requires every desired target ref to be absent (the bootstrap planner refuses targets whose desired refs exist) and deliberately ignores other stray target refs, so an aborted push or a branch deleted upstream mid-bootstrap cannot re-wedge the repo. It is gated on the source supporting batched bootstrap (protocol v2 + fetch filter); a non-batchable source stands down rather than trade a marker-anchored delta for a one-shot full pack. The reason `bootstrap-resume-marker` is threaded through dry-run, so a plan against a stranded repo confirms the routing in one shot.

**Marker lifecycle.** Prune is the marker's cleaner, and the exception that protects a live one is stated once, at prune candidacy (`addPruneCandidates`), so every plan builder is covered — including `sync --prune`, which previously would have deleted a resume position. A marker is live exactly while its branch is desired and absent; once the branch lands it is stale and prunes normally. Notably the bootstrap strategy does **not** delete the marker on the one-shot path: a nil push error doesn't prove the create landed (BestEffort swallows a per-ref `ng`), so deferring to prune costs one run and cannot be wrong. The one-shot path also passes target refs as fetch haves, so a small-repo resume transfers only the remainder.

## Behavior changes beyond the routing fix

- **`refs/gitsync/*` is no longer mirrored from a source.** Under `--all-refs`, a source ref in that namespace is now skipped by discovery. Such a ref is leftover scaffolding from that repo having been someone else's sync target, and mirroring it would collide with — and under replicate's overwrite semantics, clobber — this target's own resume marker. Consequence worth knowing: a source holding **only** that scaffolding now yields an empty desired set and errors (`no source refs matched` / `ErrNoRefsSelected`) where it previously converged. Deliberate; it clears once that source's own bootstrap resumes, which this PR is what makes possible.
- Target-side prune scope is unchanged — stale markers must stay reapable.

## Deliberately not done

- **Deletes-before-updates in `replicate.Execute`** (floated in the ticket): the update-then-delete order is load-bearing for mirror-worker's default-branch rename recovery (`cmd/worker/defaultbranch.go:67`), which relies on the replacement branch existing before entiredb rejects the current-branch delete. With routing fixed, marker cleanup no longer gates anything.
- **The `excludeRefPrefixes` stopgap in mirror-worker**: hiding `refs/gitsync/` from the sync scope would block stale-marker pruning forever, and saves no deploy.

## Known limitations — tracked in [ENT-2060](https://linear.app/entirehq/issue/ENT-2060/bootstrap-resume-partial-progress-subset-resume-and-a-sync-mode-route)

- **Partial progress doesn't resume**: a multi-branch bootstrap interrupted after one branch finalized has a non-absent desired ref, so the remainder still goes as one replicate pack (marker-anchored, but unsubdividable).
- **Sync mode has no resume route** — only its destructive half is fixed here.
- Stale markers under `--map` or branch-scoped prune have no cleaner; the batched cutover deletes its temp ref on a best-effort create too (pre-existing, same hazard class as the one fixed here); dry-run doesn't disclose marker lifecycle.

## Rollout

`vc3r` / `rci` heal once mirror-pipeline's git-sync pin is bumped past this and deployed. The companion worker change — logging `operation_mode` / `transfer_mode` / `relay_reason`, whose absence is why ENT-2054 took a code read instead of a log query — is independent and on the same-named mirror-pipeline branch.

Fast-follow to ENT-2054 (git-sync PR [#116](https://github.com/entireio/git-sync/pull/116)). That PR makes an interrupted batched bootstrap resumable from its `refs/gitsync/bootstrap/*` marker under replicate, but two shapes remain outside the resume route — both surfaced and confirmed by the PR's code review.

## 1. Partial-progress resume (the sharpened remainder of the original wedge)

`replicateBootstrapRoute` requires **all** desired target refs to be absent, because `BuildBootstrapPlans` refuses targets whose desired refs exist. A multi-branch bootstrap interrupted **after any branch finalized** (trunk done, secondary branch mid-flight) therefore can never resume batching: the remaining branch goes as one unsubdividable replicate pack. The live marker is preserved and anchors the delta (PR #116's prune guard), so the pack shrinks relative to a fresh transfer — but if the residual delta exceeds the target's pack cap, the repo wedges exactly like ENT-2054.

Fix shape: subset bootstrap — when a live marker exists and *some* desired refs are absent, route only the absent subset through the bootstrap strategy (existing target refs already serve as haves via `completedRefs`). Needs decisions on mixed-run semantics: what the Result reports, that prune is skipped for the run, and that present branches stay stale until the next delivery (a dormant upstream means no next delivery — consider a follow-up kick).

## 2. Sync mode has no resume route at all

The routing lives in the replicate-only syncer method; `sync --all-refs --prune` against a marker-bearing target still disqualifies bootstrap via `planner.CanBootstrapRelay` (prune disables it outright, `relay.go`). Same wedge shape as the original ticket, different mode. PR #116 only fixed sync mode's destructive half (its prune no longer deletes live markers, via the shared `addPruneCandidates` exception). Wants the marker routing hoisted somewhere both modes share — likely the planner.

Related: sync mode also still labels a resume `empty-target-managed-refs` (`syncer.go:953`), so the new `relay_reason` signal never reaches `sync` — the routing hoist should fix the label with it.

## 3. Batched cutover deletes its temp ref on a create it cannot confirm

`bootstrap.go` cutover (~`:687`) deletes the temp ref unconditionally, while the branch create rides the preceding best-effort push. Under `BestEffort` the pusher swallows a per-ref `ng` and returns nil (`gitproto/push.go`, `OnRejection`), so a rejected create still reaches the delete — destroying the resume position for a branch that was never created.

**Pre-existing, not a regression:** the same probe fails identically on `origin/main`. PR #116 fixed exactly this hazard on the one-shot path (by dropping strategy-side cleanup and deferring to prune, which classifies a live marker correctly); the batched path wants the same treatment, or a rejection-aware signal plumbed into the strategy. Reachable from the CLI, where `--all-refs` implies best-effort for both `bootstrap` and `sync`.

## Smaller items to sweep into whichever change touches the area

* **Stale marker under** `Mappings` **or branch-scoped prune has no cleaner**: `PruneTarget` only selects `RefKindOther` under AllRefs-without-Mappings, so an interrupted `--map` run leaves a marker that lingers forever (it no longer misroutes anything after PR #116's orphan fix — it just persists). This also means the prune backstop PR #116 relies on doesn't exist under those scopes.
* **Dry-run doesn't disclose marker lifecycle** (consistent with the batched temp-ref lifecycle, which dry-run also omits) — fold in if plan reporting is touched.
* **Reviewer suggestion**: the non-batchable-source integration test asserts the marker survives but not that it was sent as a fetch have; add the assertion if the test server grows negotiation capture.
* **Testing gotcha for whoever picks this up**: a non-nil `receivePackHook` report short-circuits the integration test server *before* it applies any command, so a hook that denies indiscriminately makes marker-lifecycle assertions vacuous. Pass ref-only pushes through (`hasPack == false` → return nil) — see `TestRun_IntegrationResumeMarkerSurvivesBestEffortRejectedCreate`.
